A pale white marble alcove, smooth and faintly luminous, a broad shaft of cool midday daylight falling from an opening above and bouncing clean white light over every egg in the clutch.
A nest in a sunny forest clearing ringed tightly with sword-ferns, the open circle of sky above pouring warm bright light down, the fern-fronds brushing the nest's outer edge in the breeze.
A moss-grown stone chamber deep in a hill, bioluminescent lichen covering the low ceiling in a soft even green glow, the nest cupped in a smooth hollow of damp ancient rock.
A nest on a warm rock-shelf beside a waterfall pool, spray misting the close air, prismatic light breaking off the falling water and scattering tiny rainbows across the bedding and eggs.
A narrow slate cave, the cleft walls dark charcoal and silver-veined, teal mineral-glow rising from a seam of strange stone just below the nest floor, cool and strange and even.
A nest at the still edge of a forest pond, lily-pads nudging the bedding, reeds standing close, soft green-filtered light lying calm and flat on the water and the clutch together.
A glacier-ice cave hollowed into deep blue ice, the walls glowing blue-white from within with filtered polar light, the nest insulated in dried sedge and feathers, cold clarity all around.
A nest tucked in a warm wildflower bank beside a drowsy stream, tall meadowsweet leaning over it, the low western sun turning the close grasses copper and the eggs a warm amber.
A copper-veined rock nook, the green and rust tracery in the stone lit by a warm amber hoard-glow from a small coin-pile wedged close, the whole hollow smelling of warm metal.
A clifftop ledge nest, close cropped turf and sea-pink cushions pressed around the eggs, the late sun low and golden on the bare rock face behind, the sea-sound rising from far below.
A deep red sandstone cave, sinuous water-worn walls curving tight around the nest, a beam of late evening sun angling in through the entrance and turning everything the colour of hot brick.

A nest pressed into the soft earth beneath a riverbank overhang, tree-roots lacing the ceiling close above, the river's green-brown reflected light rippling continuously over the eggs and the dark damp soil.
A smooth obsidian-floored lair with a low ceiling, a cluster of pale bioluminescent fungi ringing the nest and casting a quiet blue-green glow, the dark walls holding the faint warmth of deep earth.
A nest among the surface roots of a great beech tree at the wood's edge, copper leaf-litter heaped close, low autumn sun cutting sideways through bare branches and striping the clutch in pale gold.

A white marble grotto with a shallow reflecting pool just beside the nest, cool blue-white daylight entering through a low sea-arch and bouncing off the water onto the smooth pale ceiling above the eggs.
